did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 28 opens by describing humanity’s ability to find the source of silver and refine gold from the earth.
Did you know? According to the chapter, people also obtain iron from the earth and use stone and metal ores to produce copper.
Did you know? Miners are described as setting boundaries for darkness and exploring even the darkest and most remote places beneath the earth.
Did you know? The underground paths where people search for treasures are unknown to the birds of the sky; even the falcon’s eye has not seen them.
Did you know? People are described as reaching into the hard rock and overturning the roots of the mountains in search of treasures.
Did you know? After describing the search for metals and stones, the chapter asks: Where can wisdom be found, and where is the place of understanding?
Did you know? Wisdom cannot be bought with money, nor can silver be weighed out as its price.
Did you know? Wisdom is hidden from the eyes of every living creature; even the birds of the sky cannot see it.
Did you know? According to the chapter, only God understands the way to wisdom and knows where it is found.
Did you know? The chapter concludes that the wisdom by which a person should live is to fear the LORD and turn away from evil.
